data:
Ecofeminism is a school of feminism that seeks to understand intersectional nuances between
gender and environment under the patriarchal capitalist framework. The central aim of
ecofeminism is to offer an understanding of anthropocentric and androcentric worldviews on
both nature and women. As a school of feminism, ecofeminism is diverse with contradictory and
complementary perspectives about the relationship between women and nature. The course will
encompass the history, theories, and movements of ecofeminism that took place in the United
States, India, and Africa. Based on ecofeminist theories, students will examine the political,
social, and developmental impacts of ecofeminism on gender and climate change, and find
avenues for scholarly conversation in activism and research. The course will engage the students
with creative aspects of ecofeminist thoughts through literature, arts, and other creative projects.
